resultJson.description:
This is slice 4 of 4 of #8 (ADR docs/adr/0001-adr-start-spotify-from-spotify-refresh-token-fall.md). Slices 1–3 are already on this branch:
- `SpotifyTokenError`
- `SignInCodes`, the retryable browser sign-in
- `SpotifyCredentials.configuredRefreshToken`
- `SpotifyClient.signIn`, which starts from SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN and falls back to the browser on invalid_grant

The last piece of the sp_dc session cookie is still in place. `SpotifyClient.initialAuth` sends `GET https://accounts.spotify.com/authorize` with `Cookie: sp_dc=${sys.env("SPOTIFY_SP_DC")}` (src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala:76-80). That cookie is a full Spotify web session and the most sensitive secret in the setup. The browser sign-in no longer needs it: the URL is logged, and the code comes back through `callbackRoutes` → `SignInCodes.hand`.

The epic stops the app from making that request and from reading SPOTIFY_SP_DC. The proof is the whole test suite running in a forked JVM with `SPOTIFY_SP_DC=sp-dc-sentinel` set:
- A guard test checks that the fork and the variable are in place.
- A table over the three sign-in paths (valid configured token, rejected token, no token) checks that no outgoing request has a Cookie header or goes to /authorize. It also checks that the sentinel appears in no request (headers, URI or body) and in no log line.
- The existing tests that completed sign-in through a fake `/authorize` route are rewritten. Some hand the code through `SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes`, which is how the real app gets it. Others complete the `Deferred` directly where that is already the case.

Finally, README.md, .env.example and docs/how-it-works.md stop mentioning sp_dc, and the roadmap item is ticked.

Changes from the ADR:
1. Slice 4 in the ADR lists a `DocsSpec` that reads README/.env.example/how-it-works for 'sp_dc'. CLAUDE.md now forbids tests that read documentation (PR #29), so that test is not written. AC 6 is met by the docs themselves.
2. The ADR says the `Deferred` overloads of `callbackRoutes` remain, but slices 1–3 only kept the `SpotifyClient` auxiliary constructor overload. Tests wrap the `Deferred` with `SignInCodes.once(code)`, the pattern already used at SpotifyClientSpec.scala:146. No `Deferred` overload is added to main: that would be an unrequested API change.
3. The existing test "a code handed over during the authorize request is not lost" only guarded a race inside the removed /authorize request, so it is deleted rather than ported. The retry and browser sign-in tests already cover a code handed after the URL is logged.

Otherwise the program design stands: `initialAuth` = `codes.attempt` → log `Please visit: <url>` → wait for the code → code exchange, and the "Authorize" call name goes away.

tasks.title: Fork the test JVM with SPOTIFY_SP_DC set to a sentinel, plus a guard test
tasks.description:
Build changes, in build.sbt inside the `root` project's `.settings(...)` (not the model project or the Scala.js `ui` project):
- Add `Test / fork := true` and `Test / envVars += "SPOTIFY_SP_DC" -> "sp-dc-sentinel"`.
- Add a short comment saying why: the whole suite runs with the cookie variable set, so tests can show it never leaves the app.

Guard test: add a suite such as `src/test/scala/client/SpDcSentinelSpec.scala` (munit `FunSuite`) with one test asserting `sys.env.get("SPOTIFY_SP_DC") == Some("sp-dc-sentinel")`. It fails if either setting is removed: sbt's own JVM either doesn't carry the variable or carries a developer's real value.

The code still sends the cookie at this point. No existing test checks headers, so the suite stays green.

Run `sbt fix`, then `sbt check`, and confirm everything passes in the forked JVM:
- Coverage data is still collected.
- The TLS keystore (`self-signed.p12`) and `logback-test.xml` load from the classpath.

If forking surfaces a real problem, fix the cause. Don't loosen coverage or drop the fork.

tasks.title: Stop requesting /authorize with the sp_dc cookie; move tests off the fake /authorize; add the no-cookie/no-sentinel table
tasks.description:
Production, in `initialAuth` in `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala`:
- Delete the comment and the `naming("Authorize")(client.run(... Header.Raw(ci"Cookie", s"sp_dc=${sys.env.getOrElse("SPOTIFY_SP_DC", "")}")) ...)` step (lines ~76-80).
- Delete the now-unused `import org.typelevel.ci.CIStringSyntax` (line 15).
- Give `initialAuth` the ADR's doc comment: it logs the authorize URL, waits for the browser to bring the code back to the callback server, and keeps the refresh token Spotify sends.
- Nothing else in the method changes. `codes.attempt` still comes before the log line.
- Do NOT add a `callbackRoutes(Deferred)` overload. Only `callbackRoutes[F](codes: SignInCodes[F])` exists.

Tests that relied on a fake `GET /authorize` to hand over the code would now hang, so change them in the same task.

`src/test/scala/client/SpotifyClientSpec.scala`:
- "signs in on first use…" and "sign-in fails…" (lines ~105-141): before polling, hand `code-1` with `SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes[IO](SignInCodes.once(code)).orNotFound.run(Request(Method.GET, uri"/callback?code=code-1"))`. Then drop the /authorize route. `once` hands the code to the same `Deferred` that the client's auxiliary constructor wraps, so handing it before the poll works.
- `retryAfterFailedExchange`: drop its /authorize route.
- Delete the test "a code handed over during the authorize request is not lost".
- In `rig`, replace the `authorizes` counter with a recorder:
  - Wrap the whole `fake` app in an `HttpApp` that records `(method, uri, headers, body text)` and then delegates, the way `Tls.server` wraps its app (Tls.scala:28).
  - Don't record inside individual routes. Unmatched paths such as `/authorize` must be recorded too.
  - Expose the recordings on `Rig`.
  - The valid-token test's `assertEquals(authorizes, 0)` becomes a check that no recorded path is `/authorize`.

`src/test/scala/client/SpotifyTlsSpec.scala`:
- Remove the `code` parameter and the /authorize route from `fake`.
- "signing in over a trusted certificate…": before polling, hand `the-code` through `SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes[IO](SignInCodes.once(code)).orNotFound.run(...)`. Also assert that the TLS-recorded requests carry no `Cookie` header and that none has the path `/authorize`.
- "the code exchange fails…": only drop the `authorizeAnswered` wrapper and pass `Tls.redirectTo(port)(clients.spotify)` directly. Keep `code.complete("the-code")`.

Dead `GET /authorize` routes elsewhere:
- `src/test/scala/SpotifyTlsEngineSpec.scala:89`: replace the app with `HttpApp.notFound[IO]`. The test asserts `requests.size == 0`, so any app works.
- `src/test/scala/SyncEngineRunSpec.scala:344`: delete the `case GET -> Root / "authorize"` line.

New test (AC 4), in SpotifyClientSpec. It is a table over three rows. Each row runs through `rig` with `loggedAtInfo` and `TestControl.executeEmbed`, with its own client id:
- valid: `Some(token)`, answer `renewedTo("signed-in", Some("refresh-9"))`, single poll
- rejected: `Some(token)`, answer `BadRequest({"error":"invalid_grant"})`, then `browserSignIn` (start the poll, sleep, then hand; `rig` uses `SignInCodes.make`, so a code handed early is dropped)
- absent: `None`, then `browserSignIn`

For every row, assert all of the following:
- the poll plays
- no recorded request has a `Cookie` header (`headers.get(ci"Cookie")` is empty)
- no recorded request's path is `/authorize`
- the sentinel (`sys.env("SPOTIFY_SP_DC")`, failing with a clear message if unset) appears in no request's rendered headers, `uri.renderString` or body
- no captured log event's formatted message, MDC values or throwable message contains the sentinel

Which assertions fail on the current code:
- In the rejected and absent rows, the Cookie, `/authorize` and request-sentinel assertions fail on the current code, which sends `Cookie: sp_dc=sp-dc-sentinel` to /authorize. These are the proof of AC 4.
- The valid row never reaches `initialAuth`, and no log line carries the sentinel even today. Those assertions are regression guards and pass on master. Don't chase a red run for them.

Run `sbt fix` and `sbt check`.

tasks.description:
This task is documentation only, with no tests: CLAUDE.md says no test reads documentation, and AC 6 is met by the docs themselves.

- `README.md:24`: delete the `SPOTIFY_SP_DC` row from the configuration table.
- `.env.example:4`: delete the `SPOTIFY_SP_DC=` line.
- `docs/how-it-works.md` §1, mermaid diagram: replace `App->>Acc: GET /authorize (with SPOTIFY_SP_DC cookie if set)` with a step showing that the user opens the logged URL in a browser and approves, for example `Note over App,Acc: open the logged URL in a browser and approve`. The `Acc-->>CB: redirect to /callback?code=...` step that follows should still read correctly.
- `docs/how-it-works.md` §1: delete the bullet at line 31 ("If `SPOTIFY_SP_DC` is set…").
- `docs/roadmap.md` line 7 ("Replace the `sp_dc` cookie with the standard browser flow"): change `[ ]` to `[x]`. The file says "Tick items off as they land."

Afterwards, a case-insensitive search for `sp_dc` across README.md, .env.example and docs/how-it-works.md must find nothing.

The ADR under docs/adr keeps its history and is not edited. Never read or print `.env`.

resultJson.brief:
State of the branch (fix/issue-24): slices 1-3 of ADR 0001 are merged. Only the cookie request, its tests and its docs remain.

Key production file: `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala`. It is Scala 3 and colon-indented; keep that local style (the build has `-indent`).
- `class SpotifyClient[F[_]: Async: Network](client: Client[F], creds: SpotifyCredentials, session: Ref[F, Option[SpotifySession]], codes: SignInCodes[F])`. There is also an auxiliary ctor taking `Deferred[F, String]`, which wraps it in `SignInCodes.once`.
- `initialAuth: F[String]`, in order:
  - Builds `authUrl` (`https://accounts.spotify.com/authorize?client_id=…&redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:7070/callback&scope=…&state=random_<n>`).
  - Runs `codes.attempt` and logs `Please visit: $authUrl`.
  - At lines ~76-80, sends `naming("Authorize")(client.run(GET authUrl with Header.Raw(ci"Cookie", s"sp_dc=${sys.env.getOrElse("SPOTIFY_SP_DC","")}")).use(drain))`. This step and the `org.typelevel.ci.CIStringSyntax` import (line 15) are the only cookie/env code in main.
  - Waits for the code and sends `POST /api/token` with grant_type=authorization_code (call name "Code Exchange").
  - Requires a refresh_token in the answer, then calls `session.set`.
  - Logs INFO "Signed in to Spotify through the browser" with MDC client_id.
- Other members:
  - `signIn`: configured token → `refreshWith("Refresh Token Exchange")`; on Rejected, a WARN and then `initialAuth`.
  - `getOrRefresh`, `renew`, `refreshWith`, `authorised`, `getPlaybackState`, `getTempo`.
- Companion:
  - ONLY `callbackRoutes[F](codes: SignInCodes[F])` exists. There is no `Deferred` overload, despite the ADR. Wrap a `Deferred` with `SignInCodes.once(code)`, as SpotifyClientSpec.scala:146 already does, and don't add an overload to main.
  - Behaviour: GET /callback?code=… → `codes.hand(code) *> Ok("Success! Return to your terminal.")`. /callback without a code → 404.
  - Also `serverResource` and `resource`.
- `src/main/scala/client/SignInCodes.scala`: `attempt: F[F[String]]`, `hand(code): F[Boolean]`. The two constructors behave differently on timing:
  - `once(deferred)` is a single attempt over that Deferred. A code handed before the poll starts is kept. This is the pattern for the Deferred-based tests (SpotifyClientSpec ~105-141 and SpotifyTlsSpec).
  - `make` drops a hand when no attempt is pending. Tests built on `make` (`rig`, `retryAfterFailedExchange`, SyncEngineRunSpec `signingIn`) must start the poll in a fiber, `IO.sleep(1.second)` under TestControl, and only then hand the code.
- `domain.spotify.SpotifyCredentials(clientId, clientSecret, refreshToken: Option[String] = None)` with `configuredRefreshToken`. The field is an Option, not the ADR's `String = ""`. Tests write `SpotifyCredentials("id","secret", Some("tok"))`.

Tests use munit and `CatsEffectSuite`, brace syntax, no explanatory comments; the test name says what it checks.

`src/test/scala/client/SpotifyClientSpec.scala`:
- Fakes Spotify with `Client.fromHttpApp(HttpRoutes.of[IO]{…}.orNotFound)`. Routes match on path only, so the client's absolute https URLs hit `Root / "api" / "token"`, `Root / "v1" / "me" / "player"`, and so on.
- An unmatched GET /authorize just gets a 404 and is drained without failing, so removing a fake route proves nothing. Record every request by wrapping the whole app, the way `Tls.server` does at Tls.scala:28 (`HttpApp[IO](req => seen.update(req :: _) *> app.run(req))`).
- Helpers:
  - `playing` JSON
  - `renewedTo(access, refresh: Option[String])`
  - `playerFor(req)`, which accepts bearer "signed-in"
  - `rig(clientId, configured: Option[String], answer)` → `Rig(spotify, session, routes = callbackRoutes(codes).orNotFound, tokenCalls, authorizes)`, with `handCode` (GET /callback?code=browser-code)
  - `browserSignIn(r)`: start the poll, sleep 1s, hand, join
  - `loggedAtInfo = (Tls.capturedLogs, Tls.loggingAt("client.SpotifyClient", Level.INFO)).tupled`
  - `visits`, `infoLines`, `warnings`
- The rejected-token test (~line 345) already shows how to gather every log text: formatted message, MDC values and the throwable proxy message.
- Timed flows run in `TestControl.executeEmbed`.
- When recording a request body, read `req.bodyText.compile.string`. UrlForm entities built with `withEntity` are strict in http4s 0.23, so the routes can still read them with `req.as[UrlForm]`. Check that this holds; if it doesn't, rebuild the request from the recorded body before delegating.

`src/test/scala/client/SpotifyTlsSpec.scala`:
- Uses a real Ember TLS fake via `testkit.Tls.server(app)`, which returns `(port, IO[List[Request[IO]]])` and records every request that reached it.
- Clients come from `HttpClients.resource[IO]` (untrusted) or `HttpClients.trusting(Tls.selfSigned)`. `Tls.redirectTo(port)(client)` rewrites the authority to localhost:port.
- The "code exchange fails" test already completes its Deferred before polling. Its `authorizeAnswered` wrapper (lines 107-110) only kept the untrusted /authorize call from failing first.

Other test files:
- `src/test/scala/SpotifyTlsEngineSpec.scala:89` and `src/test/scala/SyncEngineRunSpec.scala:344` (in the `signingIn` helper) each contain a dead `case GET -> Root / "authorize" => Ok("login")` route.
- `HttpClientsSpec.scala:18` uses an /authorize URL only as a redirect target. Leave it alone.
- `src/test/scala/testkit/Tls.scala` provides:
  - `capturedLogs`: a ListAppender on ROOT, with events prepared for deferred processing
  - `logged(appender)`
  - `loggingAt(name, level)`
- `src/test/resources/logback-test.xml` sets root to WARN, so raise `client.SpotifyClient` to INFO to capture "Please visit".
- `DocImages` is a `runMain` object, not a suite.
- No test may read repo files outside test resources, so there is no DocsSpec.

Which new assertions fail on master: only requests from paths that reach `initialAuth` (rejected and absent tokens) carry the cookie today. No log line contains the sentinel today. The valid-row and log assertions are guards that pass on master.

Build: `build.sbt` defines three projects:
- `model`: cross JVM/JS
- `ui`: Scala.js, tests run in Node
- `root`: the app, with tests in src/test. Test-JVM settings go in root's `.settings`.

Coverage minimums are 90% statements and 85% branches overall, and 70% statements per file. Never lower them, widen `coverageExcludedPackages`, or disable Scalafix rules. `.scalafix.test.conf` applies to tests. Commands: `sbt fix` (scalafix + scalafmt), then `sbt check` (lint, clean, coverage test, aggregate), which is what CI runs.

Docs that mention sp_dc:
- README.md:24 (table row)
- .env.example:4
- docs/how-it-works.md:21 (mermaid step) and :31 (bullet)
- docs/roadmap.md:7 (open item; the file says "Tick items off as they land", so tick it `[x]`)

docs/architecture.md doesn't mention it. Leave docs/adr alone.

Secrets: never read, print or commit `.env`. The sentinel value `sp-dc-sentinel` is test-only.

resultJson.title: Stop sending the sp_dc cookie and remove SPOTIFY_SP_DC
resultJson.body:
Closes #24 (slice 4 of 4 of #8, ADR 0001).

`initialAuth` no longer requests `/authorize` with the `sp_dc` cookie, and the app no longer reads `SPOTIFY_SP_DC`. Browser sign-in is unchanged: the URL is logged and the code comes back through the callback server. `SPOTIFY_SP_DC` is removed from the README, `.env.example` and `docs/how-it-works.md`, and the roadmap item is ticked.

Tests:
- The `root` test JVM is now forked with `SPOTIFY_SP_DC=sp-dc-sentinel`. A guard test fails if the fork or the variable is missing.
- A new table test covers a valid configured token, a rejected one, and none. For each, it checks that no outgoing request has a `Cookie` header or goes to `/authorize`. It also checks that the sentinel appears in no request and no log line. The `rig` helper now records every request by wrapping the whole fake app.
- Tests that completed sign-in through a fake `/authorize` route now hand the code through `SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes`. The dead `/authorize` routes in other specs are removed.

Differences from the ADR:
- No `DocsSpec` is added, because `CLAUDE.md` forbids tests that read documentation.
- No `Deferred` overload of `callbackRoutes` is added. Tests wrap the `Deferred` with `SignInCodes.once`.
- The test "a code handed over during the authorize request is not lost" is deleted. It only covered a race inside the removed request.

The diff also includes `.orca/runs/3f6840aa6e8a.progress.json`, a run-progress file.
